about: Two Soyjaks Pointing is a simple line drawing of two bald, bearded Soyjaks with wide-open mouths. One, wearing glasses, gapes at the viewer in the foreground; the other stands behind and points excitedly at something off to the side. The blank space above them is where the object of their excitement goes. The meme mocks overexcited consumer enthusiasm: two grown men losing their minds over a franchise cameo, a new product or a reference they recognized. Over time it also became a self-aware way to admit you are genuinely hyped about something small.
origin: The drawing traces back to a 2020 photo of two men posing in front of a fast-food sign advertising plant-based fried chicken. It was redrawn as two Soyjaks and spread widely later that year.
usage:
There is one text box at the top. Put the thing they are pointing at: a logo, a character name, a product, a reference. You can also replace it with a picture when editing.

It is funniest when the trigger is very minor: a two-second cameo in a trailer, a new keyboard switch, a brand collab, the word "sequel", seeing your city mentioned in a movie. Keep the text short so it reads as the object, not a sentence.
